messages.subject: vtest is usable
parts:
Hi everyone -

The visual test system is finally in a usable state, so you should be able to use it to check if you break things while working on ggplot2. I've put it in a package that you can install via github (it's not on CRAN): https://github.com/wch/vtest

If you run into problems using it, you can file issues on the Github page. It should be usable for packages other than ggplot2, which generate ggplot2-based graphics.

Instructions: https://github.com/wch/ggplot2/wiki/Visual-test-system-instructions

Overview of how it works: https://github.com/wch/ggplot2/wiki/Visual-test-system

The test results are stored in a repository on Github, so you won't have to run the tests on each commit yourself. See the instructions wiki page for info on how to clone this repo.

At some point I'd like to set up automated testing whenever someone commits to the master branch, using a post-receive hook on Github. Essentially, when a commit is pushed to Github, Github can send out an HTTP request to some server. I'd like to set up a server that receives the request, then pulls the changes, runs the tests, and pushes the test results to Github. If anyone has experience or thoughts on setting up a server to handle this, please feel free to share.

-Winston
